claim: Gia is at 61 Van Mieu, Hanoi; smart-casual dress code; reservations require a 1,000,000 VND/diner credit-card hold refunded 10-15 business days after the visit; 48-hour cancellation policy; bookings up to 60 days in advance; experience runs ~3 hours; children under 12 not accommodated.
quote: We kindly ask guests to dress in smart casual attire... A hold of 1,000,000 VND per diner will be placed as a guarantee... Reservations can be made up to 60 days in advance... The experience takes approximately 3 hours.

claim: Gia opens Tuesday-Thursday and Sunday 18:00-22:30 for dinner only; Friday-Saturday adds lunch 11:30-14:30 (last seating 12:45) plus dinner 18:00-23:00 (last seating 20:30); closed Monday.
quote: Tuesday-Thursday & Sunday: 18:00-22:30; Friday-Saturday: 11:30-14:30 (last seating 12:45) and 18:00-23:00 (last seating 20:30)

claim: Dinner is a 10-course seasonal tasting menu priced at 3,300,000 VND per guest (≈USD 130), with optional pairings at 1,490,000 VND non-alcoholic, 1,990,000 VND alcoholic, or 2,490,000 VND wine; lunch is 8 courses at 2,500,000 VND; all prices exclude 7% service charge and VAT.
quote: Dinner: Food menu 3,300,000 VND per guest; Non-alcoholic pairings 1,490,000 VND; Alcoholic pairings 1,990,000 VND; Wine pairings 2,490,000 VND. Lunch: Food menu 2,500,000 VND per guest.

claim: Current dinner menu courses include prawn with white tea, swordfish with rice, scallop with Buddha hand, potato with salmon, flower crab with spring vegetables, bamboo shoot with wild mushroom, congee with watercress, mackerel with chili, rice with duck, and apricot/coconut dessert.
quote: prawn with white tea, swordfish with rice, scallop with Buddha hand, potato with salmon, flower crab with spring vegetables, bamboo shoot with wild mushroom, congee with watercress, mackerel with chili, rice with duck, and tomato with strawberry, concluding with apricot and coconut.

claim: Gia opened in 2020 (Sam Tran & Long Tran); received its first Michelin Star in June 2023 alongside the Michelin Young Chef Award for Sam Tran; retained the star in June 2024 and June 2025 (three consecutive years); reached 100% locally-sourced ingredients in June 2024; named to Tatler Asia's Top 100 Restaurants 2024 and Asia's 50 Best 51-100 in March 2025.
quote: June 2023: Gia was honered to receive 1 Michelin Star... June 2024: Achieved 100% locally-sourced ingredients across the menu... June 2025: Third consecutive Michelin Star recognition.

claim: Sam Tran is the first Vietnamese woman to win a Michelin star; she is self-taught, originally moved to Melbourne in 2011 as an IT master's student, switched into kitchens at Bawa Cafe and 2-hatted Sunda Dining, and returned to Hanoi to open Gia with partner Long Tran.
quote: Tran arrived in Melbourne in 2011 as a wide-eyed IT student aiming for a master's degree... she is completely self-taught and has never studied any formal cooking program... the first female chef to win a MICHELIN Star in Vietnam.

claim: Michelin inspectors describe Gia's dishes as beautifully crafted with well-judged combinations of subtle flavours where acidity and texture play prominent roles; decor draws from the Temple of Literature directly across Van Mieu Street; the name 'Gia' (family) reflects the founders' longing for home while abroad.
quote: the beautifully crafted dishes showcase well-judged combinations of subtle flavours, with acidity and texture playing prominent roles... decor draws inspiration from the Temple of Literature just across the road.

claim: Gia's interior features dark mahogany, deeply detailed emerald walls and warmly lit orb lighting; the kitchen runs a zero-waste, nose-to-tail philosophy, blending techniques the founders gathered in Australia, UAE, Thailand and Singapore with Vietnamese heritage.
quote: dark mahogany woods, deeply detailed emerald walls and warmly lit orb lighting... zero-waste, nose-to-tail philosophy... techniques from their experiences across Australia, UAE, Thailand, and Singapore.

claim: First-hand diner review: Gia occupies two floors with an upstairs dining room and glass-walled chef's table beside the kitchen; dessert is served in a separate downstairs room; atmosphere is warm modern-Vietnamese with subdued lighting and unobtrusive pop music; sommelier is notably passionate but service pacing can feel uneven.
quote: The restaurant spans two floors. The dining room upstairs features a 'chef's table' for solo diners positioned next to the kitchen, separated only by glass. Dessert is served downstairs in a separate room.

claim: Mushroom rice made from Bac Huong rice — flexible, slightly sticky, fragrant — is described as a signature dish of Gia.
quote: The mushroom rice, crafted from Bac Huong rice, takes center stage as a signature dish of Gia Restaurant. The grains are flexible, slightly sticky, and infused with a delightful fragrance.
